subject: hierarchical model with divergent transitions after warm-up.

messages.author: f6e5e26ed77eaab6
messages.subject: hierarchical model with divergent transitions after warm-up.
parts:
Dear Stan developers and users:

I posted similar questions on the forum before and I have taken some of your suggestions to use NCP hierarchical model however I still experience the problem of having divergent transitions after warm up.

A quick recap of my model, my data are intervals and thus I transform it to be a bivariate vector y_ij==(m_ij=midpoints of the intervals,  r_ij=log(range) of the intervals)  where J is the number of groups and i is the observation per group.

This bivariate vector is fitted a bivariate normal distribution, N_2(beta_j, Sigma_j)
I have some hard constraints on beta_j as all midpoints should be greater than 0, ie: beta_j1>0 and the lower bounds of the interval should also be greater than 0 which translates to a constraint on beta_j2<log(2*beta_j1)

I adopt univariate NCP on beta_j1=mu_j1+alpha_j1*sigma_j1
Declaring mu_j1, alpha_j1, sigma_j1 in the parameter block with constraints on mu_j1> -alpha_j1*sigma_j1 to ensure that beta_j1 is non-negative;
Also declaring beta_j2 to be real with constraints on its upper bound to be log(2*(mu_j1+alpha_j1*sigma_j1))

And in the transformed parameter block,
declaring beta_j1=mu_j1+alpha_j1*sigma_j1

Furthermore, I assign mu_j1~N(0,10000);
sigma_j1~cauchy(0,2.5)
alpha_j1~normal(0,1)

Also the prior on variance and covariance matrix Sigma_j is parameterised as diag(scale_j)*Omega*diag(scale_j) and follows the instructions per Rstan manual to use LKJ_corr_cholesky prior and half-Cauchy prior on scale_j.

When I run this model( 4 chains, 4000 iterations per chain), there are some numerical problems saying that the location is -inf, but it should be. 0. However, the count is small.
I think the more serious problem is that there are divergent transitions after warm up even when I increase adapt_acceptance to be 0.9999.
I have already use non-centered parameterisation and setting adapt_acceptance rate to be nearly 1, how can I fix model divergent problem in this case?
Weirdly, when I look at posterior summary, n_eff=1 for nearly all of the parameters in my model, in this case, I do not think I can trust the posterior results given divergent behaviours after warm up right?

Can someone please provide some ideas or suggestions for me to explore and fix my model?

Thanks in advance,
Jaslene

messages.author: f6e5e26ed77eaab6
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] hierarchical model with divergent transitions after warm-up.
parts:
Hi Bob:

Sorry, I meant Rhat=1 for most of the parameters. I did generate some fake data and for some situations, the posterior distributions contain the true value but for some other situations they do not.

I have attached the model and the simulated dataset. Thanks so much for looking into them.

A quick note of my model (estimating species abundance) , I have bottom 7 categories (2 observed and 5 unobserved) that directly determine top 5 categories' midpoints and log(range).

say category 12 is the highest level in my model,

its midpoints= category 11's midpoints + category 5's mipoints

its log(range)=log(2*(category 12's midpoints-category 11's midpoints-category 5's midpoints)+exp(category 11's log(range))+exp(category 5's log(range))).

In reality, I do not observe or have data on those 5 unobserved other categories, these categories are just created to absorb the differences between categories' midpoints and log(range). Hence, my first simulation is that when there is no difference between bottom and top categories then the model should estimate those 5 unobserved categories' midpoints to be very small and essentially zero range, in other words, these categories are non-existent even though I fit them in the model. This simulation, it appears that my model can recover the "true" parameters that I set.

The second simulation is where there are differences between bottom and top level's midpoints and log(range). However, in this case, the model can recover all midpoints "true" parameters but fail to estimate other unobserved categories' log(range),ie, they are still estimated to be very small and essentially zero, which means that the model estimate these categories to be single points rather than intervals.

Along with estimation problems, the model have divergent transitions after warm up and some numerical problems in chains.

Thanks again for your advice,
Jaslene
